source.description: One reviewed six-panel graphite-and-colored-pencil contact sheet cropped into five cumulative process frames and one finished master.
source.notes: Keep one empty vintage wingback chair in a stable three-quarter front view with a tall winged back, two rolled arms, one seat cushion, three visible tapered legs, two tuft buttons, piping, fabric hatching, and one broken shadow.

process_strategy: Reserve the tall back, wings, arms, cushion, apron, three visible legs, two button centers, piping, and shadow in pale construction; convert those same footprints into persistent upholstery and wood contours; stop back and apron lines behind the arms, cushion, and legs; and limit the final panel to keeper-line, graphite, and color cleanup.

rejection_checks: Keep one empty wingback chair, one three-quarter front view, one crop, and one scale in all six panels.
Keep two wings, two arms, one cushion, three visible legs, two buttons, and one broken shadow after those elements appear.
Back, seat, and apron keeper lines must stop at reserved arm, cushion, and leg silhouettes; no taught line may be erased to fake upholstery overlap.
Do not add a person, blanket, pillow, table, lamp, room, lettering, label, arrow, number, signature, watermark, or decorative border.
The final panel may not introduce an arm, cushion edge, leg, button, piping route, texture cluster, shadow shape, or color area.
The finish must look like tactile graphite and colored pencil on warm paper, not a furniture catalog rendering, glossy AI interior art, or rasterized vector illustration.
